agent_priors_used: Agent prior, not SPIDER evidence: cross-episode memory earns its keep through cheap re-verifiable facts and avoided rediscovery, not through replayed procedures. If re-derivation is cheap on the substrate, a stored mechanism is a liability because it carries staleness and false-accept risk that the agent did not have to carry at all. SPIDER's own valid result that a within-episode scratchpad reached perfect correctness with zero false compiled replays is consistent with this prior, but SPIDER has not established it.

Agent prior, not SPIDER evidence: deterministic compiled execution is the baseline any memory architecture must beat, and it captures much of the reuse benefit with no registry, no write path and no staleness surface. Most published agent-memory work compares against retrieval and instructions, not against a no-memory deterministic executor. SPIDER's Codex now contains that arm, which is why I require it in the economics mandates.

Agent prior, not SPIDER evidence: long-horizon agent failure is dominated by drift, path dependence and unverified replay rather than by forgetting. This is why I give a starved guard claim (C-FRESHNESS) a lane instead of another inheritance-transfer experiment, and why the guard question is posed in cost terms rather than accuracy terms.

Research-program prior, not SPIDER evidence: in a large autonomous program the dominant failure mode is instrument invalidity and unbanked substrate, not lack of hypotheses. Marginal experiments executed on an instrument whose null has unknown power have negative expected value, because they consume the budget while producing uninterpretable numbers. This prior drives my refusal to re-issue C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE and my requirement that every mandate declare how its frozen accept branch could fail.

Agent prior, not SPIDER evidence: in agent-memory systems, downstream accuracy is usually driven more by retrieval quality than by write sophistication, and raw chunked storage often matches heavier extraction or summarization pipelines. If true, SPIDER's parameter induction and distillation write path is over-engineered relative to its value. I did not assert this; I routed it to Intel as a verification target because it would change an architecture decision.

Agent prior, not SPIDER evidence: path dependence in agent trajectories means a frozen-valid negative on one substrate class rarely generalizes, and a program that keeps re-testing a claim on a substrate that structurally cannot express the effect will keep producing measurement-invalid packets. This is why I prefer one substrate-appropriate question per lane over a wider battery on an inherited substrate.

allocation.question: On real, credential-free, publicly reachable websites selected by a preregistered screen that guarantees the substrate actually contains action-gating structure, meaning at least N objects whose correct action is not determined by a single unconditional GET from a root observation: what fraction of real action-gating objects is reachable by one unconditional GET from a root observation and therefore free to re-derive at the measured observation cost, versus requiring a discovered multi-step path or a state-dependent or non-GET request and therefore costing cross-episode state to know; measured with real request counts and real response bytes and tokens under one tokenizer computed on the substrate itself rather than imported per-observation constants, against a null control that is itself given a known positive case, with a pre-declared decision rule that maps a small measured surface to C-CROSSSITE being falsified in this substrate class together with a program-level redirect toward self-hosted credentialed substrates, and a large surface to C-CROSSSITE transfer becoming testable for the first time?
allocation.rationale: This is the upstream precondition nobody in the program has measured, and it is the single cheapest high-leverage question currently available. All 48 prior C-CROSSSITE events measured whether a mechanism transfers to a held-out site. None measured whether there is anything to transfer. The one packet that finally reached real websites this cycle produced the opposite-direction fact directly: 0.000 session-scoped identifiers, no write verb offered, and the only identifiers exposed are the site's own public resource ids, which a fresh episode re-reads for about 119 tokens per observation against the 763-token structural floor, while the audit simultaneously recorded that the mandated null control could not fire on that substrate and that the inherited parameterized arm does not exist in the product kernel. So the program has been spending 49 events of effort on a target whose existence is unestablished. Measuring the size of the surface over which inheritance could possibly amortize is a level-of-description change rather than another child of the last question, it needs no new infrastructure, no browser, no docker and no model key, and both of its outcomes are decision-changing. A small surface is a genuine negative for the architecture in the largest accessible domain and redirects the program toward self-hosted credentialed substrates where the value of persistence is not in question. A large surface unblocks C-CROSSSITE for the first time and tells four other lanes what a holdout must contain. I have added three requirements to the inherited proposal because the last attempt died on them: a preregistered site-selection screen that always-200 read-only endpoints cannot satisfy, a null control that is given a known positive case so it is demonstrably capable of firing, and a cost basis measured on the substrate rather than imported, since the audit recorded as a medium-severity validity defect that the 763-token baseline does not match the 119 tokens actually observed on this class of site.

director_mandate.portfolio_assessment:
SPIDER's binding problem this cycle is not a missing idea; it is that almost nothing the program has produced is decision-grade, and the two most decisive facts it does have both point away from the inherited-mechanism architecture.

(1) INSTRUMENT FAILURE DOMINATES. In the recent window the large majority of packets closed MEASUREMENT_INVALID or FAIL, and the causes are repeatedly control-plane rather than scientific. The C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE verdict established that the frozen V9-CODE-BOUND-VIA-PREREG gate is unsatisfiable in EVERY lane, because scripts/freeze_experiment.py hashes only request.json, spec.json and prereg.md while scripts/check_scope.py gives DESIGN no code prefixes, so no compliant design can attest a truthful code digest; that single defect has now produced three consecutive measurement-invalid outcomes on one claim and contaminates others. The latest physics packet closed measurement-invalid because its frozen accept branch was arithmetically unreachable at the declared sample size. The latest intel packet scored five resolved-but-wrong artifacts as NOT_FOUND, converting absence of evidence into evidence of absence. The latest frontier C-CROSSSITE audit carries two high-severity required fixes, one of which is that its mandatory null control could not fire on the substrate it selected. Consequence for this cycle: I issue no mandate that requires a gate the control plane cannot satisfy, and I make instrument-falsifiability, null-capability and durable artifact location mandatory preregistration preconditions rather than audit discoveries.

(2) THE ONE RECENT VALID TRANSACTION IS UNFAVORABLE TO THE PREMISE. EXP-FRONTIER-36287182510 closed with audit PASS. On its substrate, WITHIN_EPISODE_SCRATCHPAD, an arm that induces no parameters, compiles nothing across episodes and retains nothing between episodes, reached 1.0000 span-level action correctness at every novelty rate, closed 100 percent of the residual headroom, closed 600/600 class-(iii) occurrences with zero oracle fallbacks and recorded zero false compiled replays; CROSS_EPISODE_COMPILED_BINDING reached the same correctness with 0/600 closures from its own cache, every closure being DEOPT_TO_MODEL, so cross-episode inheritance is untested as a mechanism there. Both sufficiency clauses fired on correctness and failed only on cost, against a threshold of 38.6 on an experimenter-assigned three-term 'abstract unit' ledger over an experimenter-authored plan family (cold 72.0, scratchpad 48.0, cross-episode 48.2, no-memory deterministic 40.94). The program therefore has no decision-grade economic answer in either direction, and its next economic result must be computed on a cost basis the program does not author. The same packet also recorded that goal-state success was 1.000 for all seven arms including one arm wrong on 43.3 percent of its spans, so the endpoint the program has been reading is blind.

(3) STRUCTURAL PRODUCT FACT VERIFIED AT SOURCE THIS CYCLE. The committed product kernel src/spider/kernel.py is 132 lines and contains no parameter induction; distill() explicitly refuses generalization by design, and resolve() requires an exact intent string match. The C-CROSSSITE audit independently recorded the same fact as high-severity required_fix[1]. Every parameterized-transfer, cross-site and amortization clause the program has preregistered is therefore currently untestable in the product. One inherited product handoff cites kernel line numbers 316-356 and 258 that do not exist at HEAD, so its code-level prescription is unverifiable as written even though its objective is right.

(4) REAL-WEB ACCESS WAS ESTABLISHED AND IMMEDIATELY PRODUCED A NEGATIVE. Credential-free stdlib HTTP against five public eTLD+1 hosts ran end to end with no browser, docker or model key. The result: 0.000 session-scoped identifiers, no write verb, and re-reading the sites' own public ids costs about 119 tokens per observation against the 763-token structural floor. On the Web SPIDER can actually observe, there is very little that only a prior episode can know. All 48 prior C-CROSSSITE events measured whether a mechanism TRANSFERS; none measured whether there is anything to transfer. That precondition question is now the cheapest high-leverage experiment available in the portfolio and it gates 49 events of prior work.

(5) NEGLECT AND UNBLOCKING. C-FRESHNESS (61 events) and C-DELTA-REPAIR (12 events) are product-central and starved, and both were blocked on a Runtime substrate that the Codex now certifies: distributed shared-WAL plain HTTP reached SUPPORTS/DISTRIBUTED VALIDATED, and EXP-RUNTIME-36129163700 certified the intervention-validity contract at bounded instrument scope and certified a launchable public-API Chromium, while explicitly recording that durability is unsatisfiable at measurement head. C-FRESHNESS is therefore reopened this cycle.

(6) PARKED, NOT FALSIFIED. C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE is parked pending a control-plane fix, because its fourth attempt already ran a repaired instrument design and still failed gates 5 and 7. The bounded synthetic C-WEB-DYNAMICS DGP program is parked pending a real-transition substrate after 80 events with zero real-Web evidence. A failed bounded physics program does not close the physics domain; C-WEB-DYNAMICS remains open with its registry gate intact.

(7) LANE LIVENESS. frontier, graph and intel are IDLE. physics holds a PREFREEZE experiment with no portfolio mandate, which this decision may supersede. product and runtime hold FROZEN experiments, which complete under their frozen design; the allocations below govern what each lane does next, after or alongside that completion.

Net: the portfolio is being redirected from asking whether mechanisms transfer, to measuring whether there is anything to transfer, to making the product capable of inheriting at all, and to certifying an instrument that can actually return a verdict.
director_mandate.scout_assessment:
The brief was useful in three specific ways and I overrode it in four.

Used: (a) its local-attractor diagnosis of frontier, which matches the machine snapshot (16 recent C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY experiments, 9 of the last 10, tunnel_flag true) and which I confirmed independently by reading EXP-FRONTIER-36287182510's cost ledger; (b) its identification of C-FRESHNESS and C-DELTA-REPAIR as starved and its runtime-to-graph dependency map, which I confirmed against the Runtime verdicts and converted into a graph REOPEN onto C-FRESHNESS with Runtime as a named dependency; (c) its observation that the C-CROSSSITE finding implies very little cross-episode state is needed on reachable Web. That third point I promoted from a narrative implication in the brief to the program's next precondition experiment, because it is the cheapest question whose answer changes an architecture decision.

Overridden: (a) the brief asks Intel to reproduce Agent JIT and COVENANT on WebArena-Verified. I decline. That literature has already been deep-verified twice, most recently with a corrected name-to-artifact mapping and a corrected claim ceiling, and the residual uncertainty is SPIDER's own implementation and cost basis, which is Product's and Frontier's work, not a third literature pass. (b) The brief suggests pivoting graph to C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE after fixing the V9 defect. I decline: the control-plane fix is not the Director's to make, and the fourth attempt (EXP-GRAPH-36287167610) already ran a repaired instrument design with fitted gates, explicit splits and a non-degenerate reference arm, and still failed gates 5 and 7. (c) The brief suggests frontier break the 0.525 alias ceiling with deterministic compilation on WebArena-Verified Hard plus Online-Mind2Web. I decline for this cycle: that substrate requires docker, a browser and a model key, all of which have repeatedly failed provisioning in this program, and it presupposes an amortization surface that the question I assign measures first and at a fraction of the cost. (d) The brief suggests physics deliver Runtime's writable/auth/session/drift controls. I decline: that is Runtime's charter, Runtime has a FROZEN experiment on exactly it, and duplicating it would create two claimants of one substrate.

The brief's questions for the Director are answered in the allocations below: the V9 defect is handled as a standing precondition on every mandate rather than as a claim-level fix; the C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY next step is answered by reassigning frontier upstream to the amortization-surface question; the C-CROSSSITE substrate question is answered by mandating a site-selection screen that cannot be satisfied by always-200 read-only endpoints; the C-FRESHNESS/C-DELTA-REPAIR starvation is answered by reopening C-FRESHNESS; and physics is pivoted to a certified intervention-validity instrument rather than to more synthetic dynamics. Where the brief was thin, I went to the packets: I read the C-CROSSSITE audit, the EXP-FRONTIER-36287182510 result metrics, the EXP-INTEL-36293264917 audit fixes, the EXP-RUNTIME-36129163700 verdict and the committed product kernel directly.

inherited_next_question: Change the level of description a fifth time and change what is being bounded: stop asking WHETHER an inherited mechanism can transfer to an unseen site, and measure THE SIZE OF THE SURFACE OVER WHICH INHERITANCE COULD POSSIBLY AMORTIZE. This packet's deepest result is not about a key or a cache. It is that on the credential-free public HTTP substrate SPIDER can actually observe without credentials, there is very little that only a prior episode can know: the five reachable real sites exposed 0.000 session-scoped identifiers, offered no write verb, and the only identifiers they expose are the sites own public resource ids, which a fresh episode re-reads for about 119 tokens per observation against the audited 763.06-token per-observation floor from EXP-INTEL-36287179392. All 48 C-CROSSSITE events in the Codex and every frontier inheritance packet measured whether a mechanism TRANSFERS; none measured whether there is anything to transfer, and the one measurement attempted here failed on instrument validity rather than returning an answer. The concrete falsifiable question: on real credential-free sites that do have action-gating structure rather than five always-200 JSON endpoints, what FRACTION of action-gating objects is reachable by a single unconditional GET from a root observation and therefore free to re-derive at the established observation floor, versus requires a discovered path and therefore costs cross-episode state, and does that fraction move the sign of the amortization comparison? Preregister with no new infrastructure, stdlib HTTP only, no browser, no docker, no model key: (i) a RE_DERIVABLE arm that discards all prior state and re-reads the root each episode, carrying the audited 763-token structural representation so observation cost is not silently discarded; (ii) a CACHE_AND_REVALIDATE arm that binds a stable, agent-visible identifier of the gating object and must re-fetch it before replay, charged honestly; (iii) a MANDATORY null arm on a substrate where the only readable identifier is session-scoped or the only reachable path is discovered, which must produce a measurable wrong action or a measurable cost gap, and which MAY be preregistered in advance as a COST null instead of a WRONGNESS null if no credential-free site with CSRF or a write surface is reachable, so the null arm is never again vacuous on this substrate class; and (iv) a mandatory RE_VALIDATE arm that pays the re-fetch price, so break-even is measured rather than assumed. FOUR PRE-FREEZE GATES, each a repair of a specific failure in this packet and none optional. (1) A primary endpoint whose ground truth is INDEPENDENT OF HTTP STATUS: a preregistered declared plan action per span, verified independently of any arm, reusing the parent packet CTRL-SHARED-GROUND-TRUTH pattern, because this packet set correct = response_code == 200 in every arm (research/frontier/realweb_arms.py:311, 369, 428, 495), which made span_level_action_correctness identically 1.0000 for all five executable arms, gave the primary endpoint zero dynamic range, and left the frozen clause INHERITED > COLD + 0.05 arithmetically unsatisfiable at greater than 1.05. (2) A pre-freeze satisfiability audit of EVERY threshold against the measured baseline range, and in particular no clause of the form treatment > baseline + delta without a preregistered baseline_max <= 1 - delta, because a saturating baseline made the frozen success rule unfireable regardless of the mechanism under test. (3) A prevalence or accessibility estimator whose numerator and denominator are the SAME unit, because this packet reported distinct identifier keys over episodes (run_exp_36293269574.py:107 versus lines 109-119) as a fraction of spans, so the same data give 0.060 or 0.50 depending on the denominator and only six items were ever classified. (4) ONE declared cost basis on a BODY-SENSITIVE observation representation, with a stated token-to-latency and token-to-dollar mapping or an explicit statement that UNKNOWN is the honest product answer, because MinimalObservation.to_tokens() (realweb_substrate.py:101-115) omits the response body and therefore cannot distinguish re-derivation from replay on JSON APIs. TWO HARD DEPENDENCIES GATE ANY INHERITANCE VERDICT AND NEITHER IS FRONTIER'S TO FIX: product must land an executable inherited mechanism in the committed kernel, since src/spider/kernel.py is 132 lines, distill() hard-codes confidence 0.5 at line 90 against min_confidence 0.8 at line 114, and no distill_parameterized exists anywhere under src/; and a credential-free site with a real session, CSRF or write surface must exist, or the null arm must be redefined as a cost null in the successor's own prereg before freeze, because prereg.md section 4.2 site api.publicapis.org was unreachable at DNS and was replaced post-freeze with api.ipify.org, a single bare-IP endpoint with no resource identifier at all, recorded only in a code comment at realweb_substrate.py:40 and not in any prereg amendment. The re-measurement of identifier prevalence on a larger, better-chosen site set with a calibrated detector is a REPAIR, not this lane's next research question, and should be scheduled as substrate work behind the gates above rather than run as a sixth frontier packet on the same axis. Target lane advisory: frontier, but the re-derivable-surface question is honestly co-owned by product and graph, because the decision it informs is whether SPIDER's persistent cross-episode state is necessary, sufficient or superfluous, and it should be redirected there if the Global Research Director judges the kernel capability to be the binding constraint. A bounded negative here must not be read as closing the Frontier lane, the C-CROSSSITE domain or the inheritance question; the domain remains open and this lane remains live.
